data.analysis: The three roles cover useful independent knobs, but the plan risks assuming threading pays off, that the frozen build enables useful SIMD, and that source-level repeated sqrtf calls survive compiler optimization. T2 and T3 both touch the arithmetic kernel; distinguish explicit lane-level SIMD from scalar algebraic rewrites, and measure each T3 rewrite independently before combining. Add a compiler-vectorized loop as a contrast to explicit intrinsics in T2. Keep all roles and N unchanged; any speedup remains a hypothesis until correctness and compatible measurements support it.

revisions.objective: In src/candidate.cpp, compare the serial baseline with an OpenMP outer loop using the passed threads value as a hard CPU budget; start with static scheduling and retain a serial path for one thread or small n. Avoid thresholds tied to published test values. Measure available valid n/thread cases under the frozen protocol, verify complete output writes and varied-input correctness, and report overhead as well as any gain. Preserve correct variants for later combination even if they lose in isolation.
revisions.subject: OpenMP scaling and overhead within the threads budget

revisions.objective: Keep threading unchanged and compare the ordinary per-option loop as compiled by the frozen build with an explicit x86-intrinsics kernel. Use only ISA supported by the frozen target/build, with compile-time guards and a scalar fallback; do not change compiler flags or add runtime environment/ISA probing. Preserve the supplied Black-Scholes computation and CND coefficients. If vector math requires altered rounding, validate it against tolerance on varied inputs and retain a correct fallback. Measure each route separately so G can test combinations with T1 and T3.
revisions.subject: Compiler-vectorized versus explicit SIMD execution

revisions.objective: Keep this tree scalar-focused. Test sharing sqrtf(T) and Horner evaluation of the supplied CND polynomial as separate changes and in combination; preserve the formula and coefficients, and validate rounding on varied inputs. Judge changes by measured correctness and time rather than assuming the compiler does or does not already combine operations. Retain correctness-passing rewrites that are slightly slower alone if they could enable a later measured combination with T1 or T2.
revisions.subject: Isolated scalar arithmetic rewrites and combination candidates

data.shared_assumptions: The supplied source is serial and the baseline is valid, but its three timing samples alone do not establish scaling behavior or the dominant cost; n and call-time thread distributions are unspecified. Target and compiler are supplied, while enabled ISA/compiler flags are not. The compiler may already common repeated expressions. Only the input base is stated 64-byte aligned, so array offsets may not be. Preserve all per-element work, the supplied CND coefficients, output coverage, and tolerance; compare only correctness-passing programs using the frozen protocol.
